name: Coastal Strip and Highlands
inspired_by: The Gaza Strip and the West Bank as of October 2026, built as two separate sectors on one zone graph because one contiguous map cannot hold both. Sector A follows the Gaza situation after the October 2025 ceasefire: a narrow, extremely dense coastal strip with very heavy war damage, displaced families in tent areas near the coast, and the eastern part held by Israeli forces behind a demarcation line. Sector B follows the northern West Bank hill country: olive-terraced limestone hills, Palestinian towns and refugee camps, Israeli settlements and military posts, checkpoints and the separation barrier, with the Jordan Valley at its east edge. Every town and camp is fictional; no real place is reproduced.
map_layout_note: Two sectors share one map file: Sector A (coastal strip) is 7 x 16 km on the west; Sector B (highlands) is 12 x 16 km on the east; a 1 km impassable seam separates them, and the zone graph links them only through off-map travel (proposed).
climate: Mediterranean (Koppen Csa) on the coast and in the hills; semi-arid to arid (BSh/BWh) in the Jordan Valley. Coast: 25-32 C summers, 12-18 C winters, 300-400 mm rain. Hills: 28-30 C summers, cold wet winters with 500-700 mm rain and occasional snow above 800 m. Jordan Valley: very hot (40 C+) summers below sea level.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb): storms flood low ground and tent areas on the coast; cold rain and fog in the hills
Spring (Mar-May): short green season, hamsin dust and heat days
Summer (Jun-Sep): humid heat on the coast, dry heat in the hills, water shortage
Autumn (Oct-Nov): olive harvest across the hills, first rains

vegetation: ancient olive groves on dry-stone terraces
thorny burnet and thyme on bare slopes
desert steppe shrubs on the eastern slopes
date palm plantations and banana in the valley
tamarisk and reeds along the river

terrain.relief: Sector A: almost flat sand and loess coastal plain at 0-80 m with low dune ridges and a shallow wadi crossing it. Sector B: rugged limestone hills at 400-920 m with steep valleys, dropping east over 10 km down rough eastern slopes to the Jordan Valley floor at about -300 m.
features: a shallow wadi with a polluted stream crossing Sector A
tunnel network as level geometry under Sector A towns
the separation barrier (concrete wall in towns, fence elsewhere) along Sector B's west edge
steep wadis down to the Jordan Valley
terrain.water: Mediterranean along Sector A's west edge; brackish groundwater, damaged desalination and wells; springs and rainwater cisterns in the hills; the Jordan River as a narrow, reed-lined river on Sector B's east edge.

generator.approach: Two independent heightmaps. Sector A: near-flat coastal plain with dune noise and a wadi spline; urban fabric placed first, then a destruction pass (see notes). Sector B: west-high to east-low tilt with hills from fbm and ridged noise, terraces quantised on 8-30 degree slopes, and a strong east escarpment ramp down to the valley.

noise_layers.purpose: Sector A coastal dunes and low ridges
Sector B east escarpment to the Jordan Valley over the last 5 km
micro-relief, rubble mounds (Sector A), boulders (Sector B)

generator.erosion: Sector A none (flat). Sector B hydraulic erosion (50 iterations) to cut eastward wadis; terraces post-pass in olive zones.
generator.rivers: Sector A: one wadi spline west to the sea, 30-80 m wide, shallow. Sector B: wadis by flow accumulation; Jordan River spline along the east edge, 10-30 m wide, meandering.
generator.settlement_flattening: Sector A towns flattened to the plain; Sector B towns per plot along slopes, settlements on flattened hilltops with retaining walls.
generator.notes: Destruction pass for Sector A (game-level, factual scale): 50-80% of structures in Sector A towns are damaged or collapsed, generated by removing slabs and walls with a noise mask; collapsed buildings become rubble mounds that are traversable but slow. Tunnel shafts are POI-stamped into structures as level geometry only.

settlements.architecture: Sector A: four- to twelve-storey reinforced-concrete apartment buildings with cinder-block infill, flat roofs with water tanks and solar panels, ground-floor shops with steel shutters; most heavily damaged, with pancaked slabs, open facades and rubble streets; displaced families living in damaged buildings and in tents in cleared lots.
settlements.wall_class: Standing concrete frames thick; infill thin; rubble mounds medium cover; tents none.
layout_rules: grid of main roads (a north-south coastal road and a central highway) with dense side streets
destruction mask 50-80% (higher near the demarcation line)
cleared lots and squares hold tents and aid points
hospitals, schools and mosques as landmarks and shelters
extremely high civilian density

settlements.architecture: Two kinds. Sector A coastal tent areas: improvised tents of tarpaulin, nylon and wood, aid tents, water points, makeshift latrines on sand. Sector B refugee camps from the 1950s: very dense three- to five-storey concrete houses on tiny plots, alleys 1-2 m wide, murals, rooftop water tanks; parts bulldozed by 2025 military operations and partly emptied.
settlements.wall_class: Tents none; camp houses 15-20 cm block thin (breachable but few routes).
layout_rules: tent areas: irregular rows on sand along the coast, water and food distribution points
camp alleys: no vehicle access beyond the main street; bulldozed roads cut through parts
a UN school and clinic as landmarks
very high civilian density

settlements.wall_class: Stone-clad concrete thick; old-core 60-90 cm stone thick and vaulted; infill thin.

infrastructure.roads: Sector A: one coastal road and one central highway north-south, heavily damaged, with cleared lanes; east-west roads cut by the demarcation line. Sector B: a bypass road network linking settlements, older village roads, agricultural tracks; road gates and closures.
infrastructure.power: Sector A: grid largely down; generators, solar panels and a damaged power plant. Sector B: overhead lines, frequent cuts in towns.
infrastructure.ports: Sector A: small fishing harbour (damaged); an aid jetty proposal is not modelled. LHD use is restricted (see insertion).
infrastructure.checkpoints: Sector A: demarcation-line posts; the southern crossing to Egypt and the eastern goods crossing for aid. Sector B: permanent checkpoints at town entrances, flying checkpoints, road gates, the separation barrier, the Jordan River crossing at the east edge.

conditions: winter storms flooding low ground and tents
weather.visibility_notes: Dust from rubble and hamsin days lowers visibility in Sector A; hill fog in Sector B winters. Very dark Sector A nights (no grid power) favour NVGs; Sector B towns are lit.
weather.dust_or_snow: Rubble dust year-round in Sector A; rare snow on the highest Sector B ridges.

civilians.behaviour: Sector A: the densest civilian map in the game. People queue at water and aid points from dawn, move along cleared roads on foot and by cart, and shelter in damaged buildings and tents; gunfire causes crowds to scatter toward buildings, not away from them. Sector B: busy towns and markets (08:00-15:00), traffic queues at checkpoints, farmers in olive groves in autumn; raids empty streets but people stay at home.
vehicles: yellow-plate and green-plate private cars (Sector B)
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Casualty penalties apply in full and dominate play: Sector A contracts are mostly escort and recovery with strict fire discipline; any firefight near tents, aid points or hospitals is likely to void the contract.

factions_present.where: Sector A towns and camps west of the demarcation line, tunnel shafts in damaged quarters; low in Sector B (small cells in towns).
Sector A camps (small rocket and drone teams); Sector B refugee-camp alleys (small, largely broken-up cells).
Sector A east of the demarcation line (posts, cleared buffer); Sector B checkpoints, settlement security, military posts and raids into camps and towns; drones over both sectors.
Sector B towns (Area A-type): security compound, police posts, polling stations; a trained police unit staging at the Sector A southern crossing.
Sector A southern crossing and border fence; aid convoy staging on the far side.
Sector B Jordan River crossing at the east edge; aid convoys from Jordan.

frontline: Sector A: the demarcation line is the frontline. In the ceasefire state it is static and the war sim posts escort, distribution, UXO and remains-recovery contracts; violation events (incidents near the line, rocket or drone launches) raise the alert in nearby zones and can shift the line a few hundred metres for days. A disarmament-progress meter (proposed) slowly lowers hamas strength in Sector A when verification contracts succeed and a phased-withdrawal event moves the line east. Sector B: no front; zones flip between calm and raid states. Raids on camps by isr and arrest operations by pse_pa reduce pij and hamas cells; settler-village tension events post neutral escort contracts. The election (late November 2026 in the campaign calendar) posts pse_pa security contracts.
contract_hooks: Aid convoy escort from the southern crossing to a distribution point (clients egy, jor, isr; strict rules of engagement)
Secure polling stations in a Sector B town during the legislative election (client pse_pa)
VIP protection for officials between the security compound and a crossing (client pse_pa)
Train and accompany a police unit on a UXO-clearance day (clients pse_pa, egy)
Clear UXO hazards in a rubble quarter with engineers (client pse_pa)
Hostage or remains-recovery intel follow-up near the demarcation line (client isr; intel only)
Border security and anti-smuggling patrol at the southern crossing (client egy)
Defend an aid convoy against an ambush by an armed cell or looters in a damaged district (any convoy client)

hot_zones.layout: hamas command node in a tunnel-shaft quarter; 3-4 outposts in damaged blocks; aid-route checkpoints; roaming 2-4 man cells and drone teams; demarcation-line posts as the third party. Proposed only for late in the early game, given the civilian density.

insertion.fob: Coastal map but LHD operations are restricted by the client (proposed: LHD only for evacuation contracts via the fishing harbour). Normal entry is by road through the southern crossing (Sector A) or the Jordan River crossing (Sector B), from a FOB on the far side of each crossing; helicopters only for medical evacuation.

early_game_notes: hamas and pij are early-tier (pij is the lowest-ramp enemy in the game), but civilian density is extreme, so early contracts here should be escort, election security and UXO work rather than raids.
